accepted.s:
With reference to the Index of Core Industries (ICI), consider the following statements:
1. It is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser under the DPIIT.
2. The revised series of the ICI has 2022-23 as its base year.
3. Iron ore was added to the revised series with a weight of 4.905 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The ICI is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT. The revised series uses 2022-23 as the base year and includes iron ore with a weight of 4.905 per cent.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional-identity and numerical clues together before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Eight core industries - list, combined weight in IIP, highest weight sector

accepted.s: Under the revised 2022-23 series of the Index of Core Industries, which one of the following has the highest weight?
accepted.x: Electricity carries the highest weight in the revised series, at 30.93 per cent. Refinery products have the second-highest weight at 22.57 per cent.
accepted.tq: Compare the revised weights rather than relying on the older series.
accepted.sec: Eight core industries - list, combined weight in IIP, highest weight sector

accepted.s: What is the combined weight of the eight core industries in the old 2011-12 series of the Index of Industrial Production?
accepted.x: The eight core industries together accounted for 40.27 per cent of the IIP in the old 2011-12 series. In the revised series, the nine industries have a combined weight of 32.88 per cent.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the old combined weight from the revised combined weight.
accepted.sec: Eight core industries - list, combined weight in IIP, highest weight sector

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the number of industries and the combined IIP weight under the revised 2022-23 series of the Index of Core Industries?
accepted.x: The revised series contains nine core industries and their combined weight in the IIP is 32.88 per cent. Iron ore was added to the earlier list of eight industries.
accepted.tq: Split the option into two parts and verify both the count and the percentage.
accepted.sec: Eight core industries - list, combined weight in IIP, highest weight sector

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs relating to the revised Index of Core Industries:
1. Electricity — 30.93 per cent
2. Refinery products — 22.57 per cent
3. Steel — 17.58 per cent
4. Fertilisers — 2.73 per cent
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched under the revised 2022-23 series. Fertilisers have the lowest weight among the nine core industries.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical pair independently before using the coded options.
accepted.sec: Eight core industries - list, combined weight in IIP, highest weight sector

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct descending order of the old 2011-12 weights of the core industries, beginning with the highest?
accepted.x: In the old series, refinery products had the highest weight at 28.04 per cent, followed by electricity at 19.85 per cent, steel at 17.92 per cent and coal at 10.33 per cent.
accepted.tq: Watch for reversal of the top two sectors between the old and revised series.
accepted.sec: Eight core industries - list, combined weight in IIP, highest weight sector

accepted.s: With reference to the revised methodology of the Index of Core Industries, which of the following statements is correct?
o: It counts coking coal alone and uses net steel output.
It counts raw coal only and uses gross steel output.
It counts imported coal and uses net steel output.
It excludes coal and uses finished steel output only.
accepted.x: The revised methodology counts only raw coal and uses gross steel output. These methodological changes apply to the revised core industries series.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between paired technical terms such as raw/gross and coking/net.
accepted.sec: Eight core industries - list, combined weight in IIP, highest weight sector

accepted.s: The Index of Core Industries recorded a growth of approximately what percentage in June 2026 under the new series?
accepted.x: The ICI grew by 5 per cent in June 2026, which was described as a five-month high. Iron ore growth was the major driver at 43.9 per cent.
accepted.tq: Separate the monthly ICI figure from the figures for February and July 2026.
accepted.sec: Eight core industries - list, combined weight in IIP, highest weight sector

accepted.s: In June 2026, which core industry was identified as the principal driver of the growth of the Index of Core Industries?
accepted.x: Iron ore drove the June 2026 ICI growth, recording an increase of 43.9 per cent. The revised series had been expanded to include iron ore.
accepted.tq: Link the exceptional growth rate with the sector responsible for it.
accepted.sec: Eight core industries - list, combined weight in IIP, highest weight sector

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Index of Industrial Production (IIP):
1. It is a composite indicator of short-term changes in the volume of industrial production.
2. It measures changes against a specified base period.
3. It covers mining, manufacturing and electricity.
4. It includes agriculture, services and construction activity as its broad sectors.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The IIP measures short-term changes in industrial production relative to a base period and covers mining, manufacturing and electricity. Agriculture, services and construction activity are outside its coverage.
accepted.tq: Find the false inclusion statement by distinguishing industrial sectors from excluded activities.
accepted.sec: Eight core industries - list, combined weight in IIP, highest weight sector

accepted.s: The base year of the Index of Industrial Production was revised from 2011-12 to:
accepted.x: The new IIP series uses 2022-23 as its base year instead of 2011-12. The revision was released in June 2026.
accepted.tq: Use the base-year pair as a direct numerical recall question.
accepted.sec: Eight core industries - list, combined weight in IIP, highest weight sector

accepted.s: The revised series of the Index of Industrial Production with 2022-23 as its base year applies retrospectively from:
accepted.x: The revised IIP series with the 2022-23 base year applies from April 2023. The Wholesale Price Index base was also revised to 2022-23 at the same time.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the release date from the date from which the series applies.
accepted.sec: Eight core industries - list, combined weight in IIP, highest weight sector

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a use-based group in the Index of Industrial Production?
accepted.x: The IIP use-based groups include primary goods, capital goods, intermediate goods, infrastructure and construction goods, consumer durables and consumer non-durables. Agricultural services are not an IIP use-based group.
accepted.tq: Identify the option outside the established classification rather than choosing a familiar industrial category.
accepted.sec: Eight core industries - list, combined weight in IIP, highest weight sector

accepted.s: In the 2011-12 series of the IIP, which use-based category had the highest and which had the lowest weight respectively?
accepted.x: Primary goods had the highest weight at about 34 per cent, while capital goods had the lowest weight at 8.22 per cent in the 2011-12 series.
accepted.tq: Pair the maximum and minimum values instead of considering either value in isolation.
accepted.sec: Eight core industries - list, combined weight in IIP, highest weight sector

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly matches the indicator with its growth rate for FY 2024-25?
o: IIP — 5.2 per cent; ICI — 2.3 per cent
IIP — 4.0 per cent; ICI — 5.2 per cent
IIP — 4.0 per cent; ICI — 4.5 per cent
IIP — 4.5 per cent; ICI — 4.0 per cent
accepted.x: In FY 2024-25, the IIP grew by 4.0 per cent and the ICI grew by 4.5 per cent. The 5.2 per cent and 2.3 per cent figures relate to IIP and ICI respectively in February 2026.
accepted.tq: Match each rate with its correct indicator and period before eliminating reversed pairs.
accepted.sec: Eight core industries - list, combined weight in IIP, highest weight sector

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. In FY 2024-25, manufacturing grew faster than electricity within the IIP components.
2. In FY 2024-25, mining grew by 3.0 per cent.
3. In July 2026, coal growth was 7.6 per cent.
4. In July 2026, iron ore growth was 29.5 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statement 1 is false because manufacturing grew by 4.1 per cent in FY 2024-25, below electricity growth of 5.2 per cent. Mining grew by 3.0 per cent, while July 2026 coal and iron ore growth was 7.6 per cent and 29.5 per cent respectively.
accepted.tq: Compare rates within the same period and reject the reversed growth relationship.
accepted.sec: Eight core industries - list, combined weight in IIP, highest weight sector

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the February 2026 IIP and ICI growth rates?
o: IIP 5.2 per cent and ICI 2.3 per cent
IIP 6.0 per cent and ICI 5.2 per cent
IIP 4.0 per cent and ICI 4.5 per cent
IIP 2.3 per cent and ICI 5.2 per cent
accepted.x: In February 2026, IIP growth was 5.2 per cent and ICI growth was 2.3 per cent. Manufacturing within the IIP grew by 6 per cent.
accepted.tq: Keep the two closely related indices paired with their respective monthly rates.
accepted.sec: Eight core industries - list, combined weight in IIP, highest weight sector

accepted.s: Which of the following sectors outpaced the core sectors in February 2026?
accepted.x: In February 2026, non-core manufacturing and capital goods outpaced the core sectors. This indicates stronger performance outside the core-industry grouping during that month.
accepted.tq: Identify the comparative relationship rather than recalling an isolated growth percentage.
accepted.sec: Eight core industries - list, combined weight in IIP, highest weight sector

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the change in India's sectoral GDP structure after 1991?
o: All three major sectors gained equal shares.
Industry gained the most share relative to services.
Agriculture gained the most share relative to services.
Services gained the most share, while industry's share did not rise significantly relative to services.
accepted.x: After 1991, the services sector gained the most share in GDP. Industry did not rise significantly in share relative to services.
accepted.tq: Avoid the reversal trap between industry and services in structural-change questions.
accepted.sec: Industrial structure changes since 1991 - share of industry in GDP, manufacturing vs construction, private sector share

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about India's industrial structure since 1991:
1. Post-LPG growth favoured capital- and skill-intensive sectors.
2. Automobiles, specialty chemicals, pharmaceuticals and IT hardware benefited from this pattern.
3. Auto components and pharmaceuticals became part of global value chains.
4. Services lost the greatest share of GDP after 1991.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because services gained the most GDP share after 1991.
accepted.tq: Use the sectoral-trend statement to eliminate the otherwise correct-looking combination containing a reversed trend.
accepted.sec: Industrial structure changes since 1991 - share of industry in GDP, manufacturing vs construction, private sector share

accepted.s: Industry accounts for approximately what share of Gross Value Added in India?
accepted.x: Industry accounts for approximately 25.3 per cent of GVA. The 13–14 per cent figure relates to the public sector's contribution to GDP, while 17–18 per cent refers to manufacturing's real-term share.
accepted.tq: Separate similar percentages by linking each figure to its correct economic aggregate.
accepted.sec: Industrial structure changes since 1991 - share of industry in GDP, manufacturing vs construction, private sector share

accepted.s: Why did manufacturing's share of nominal GVA decline despite its real-term share remaining broadly stable?
o: Because the private sector withdrew from manufacturing
Because construction was excluded from GVA
Because manufacturing output ceased to grow after 1991
accepted.x: The decline in manufacturing's nominal GVA share was attributed to relative price changes. In real terms, manufacturing's share remained broadly steady at 17–18 per cent.
accepted.tq: Distinguish nominal changes caused by prices from real changes in output.
accepted.sec: Industrial structure changes since 1991 - share of industry in GDP, manufacturing vs construction, private sector share

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the FY26 growth rates of manufacturing and services?
o: Manufacturing 7.0 per cent and services 9.1 per cent
Manufacturing 4.1 per cent and services 9.1 per cent
Manufacturing 7.0 per cent and services 4.1 per cent
Manufacturing 9.1 per cent and services 7.0 per cent
accepted.x: In FY26, manufacturing growth was 7.0 per cent, whereas services growth was 9.1 per cent. Thus, services grew faster than manufacturing.
accepted.tq: Check both sector and rate before accepting a growth comparison.
accepted.sec: Industrial structure changes since 1991 - share of industry in GDP, manufacturing vs construction, private sector share

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding manufacturing and industry in FY26:
1. The share of medium- and high-tech manufacturing was 46.3 per cent.
2. Industry GVA grew by 7.0 per cent in the first half of FY26.
3. Manufacturing GVA grew by 9.13 per cent in the second quarter of FY26.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Medium- and high-tech manufacturing accounted for 46.3 per cent, industry GVA grew 7.0 per cent in H1 FY26, and manufacturing GVA grew 9.13 per cent in Q2 FY26.
accepted.tq: Retain the period attached to each figure, especially H1 and Q2.
accepted.sec: Industrial structure changes since 1991 - share of industry in GDP, manufacturing vs construction, private sector share

accepted.s: The public sector contributes approximately what share of India's GDP, implying that the private sector dominates industrial output?
accepted.x: The public sector contributes about 13–14 per cent of GDP. Consequently, the private sector dominates industrial output.
accepted.tq: Connect the numerical share with the conclusion about sectoral dominance.
accepted.sec: Industrial structure changes since 1991 - share of industry in GDP, manufacturing vs construction, private sector share

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the contribution of MSMEs to the Indian economy?
o: 31.1 per cent of GDP, 35.4 per cent of manufacturing output and 48.58 per cent of exports
35.4 per cent of GDP, 31.1 per cent of manufacturing output and 48.58 per cent of exports
31.1 per cent of GDP, 48.58 per cent of manufacturing output and 35.4 per cent of exports
48.58 per cent of GDP, 35.4 per cent of manufacturing output and 31.1 per cent of exports
accepted.x: MSMEs contribute 31.1 per cent of GDP, 35.4 per cent of manufacturing output and 48.58 per cent of exports. The figures represent three different economic contributions.
accepted.tq: Match each percentage to the correct aggregate instead of treating the figures as interchangeable.
accepted.sec: Industrial structure changes since 1991 - share of industry in GDP, manufacturing vs construction, private sector share

accepted.s: Approximately how many jobs were added in organised manufacturing between 2015-16 and 2024-25?
accepted.x: About 57 lakh jobs were added in organised manufacturing between 2015-16 and 2024-25. The figure of 56.2 crore refers to total employment in Q2 FY26.
accepted.tq: Distinguish lakh-level sectoral job creation from crore-level total employment.
accepted.sec: Industrial structure changes since 1991 - share of industry in GDP, manufacturing vs construction, private sector share

accepted.s: The total employment reported for the second quarter of FY26 was approximately:
accepted.x: Total employment was reported at approximately 56.2 crore in Q2 FY26. This is distinct from the 57 lakh jobs added in organised manufacturing over the 2015-16 to 2024-25 period.
accepted.tq: Read the unit carefully and avoid confusing total employment with incremental employment.
accepted.sec: Industrial structure changes since 1991 - share of industry in GDP, manufacturing vs construction, private sector share
